chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halby, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Every oath not intended for the Sake of Allah, the Exalted, regarding a divorce or freeing a slave, is not valid.

key_terms.وَجْهُ اللَّهِ: The Face of Allah (intention for His sake)

ai.seo_question: When is an oath regarding divorce or freeing a slave considered invalid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the condition of sincerity (ikhlas) in oaths intended to effectuate divorce or manumission, asserting that such oaths are null if the intent is not for Allah's sake. In Shia jurisprudence, this underscores the principle that the spiritual validity of the oath is tied to the intention, distinguishing it from mere verbal utterance. It serves as a key text for understanding how personal intent impacts the legal efficacy of conditional statements in family law.
